title: Date and nut energy balls
summary: Four ingredients, one blender, no baking. Dates do the sticking and the sweetening, so there is no sugar in here at all.

ingredients.note: These are the glue, not just the sweetener - a zero-calorie sweetener cannot replace them here.
Add 1 tbsp water with it, or the mix goes dry and crumbly.
Not optional. Unsalted date balls taste flat.

steps: If your dates are dry or hard, soak them in hot water for 10 minutes, then drain properly.
Blitz the almonds and oats alone first, to a coarse meal. Doing this before the wet ingredients go in stops you ending up with nut butter.
Add the dates, peanut butter, cocoa, salt and vanilla. Blend in pulses, scraping down the sides, until it clumps together and pulls away from the walls.
Squeeze a bit in your palm. If it holds, it is ready. If it crumbles, add one more date or a teaspoon of water and pulse again.
Roll into 12 balls, then roll in desiccated coconut if you want.
Chill 30 minutes to firm up. They keep two weeks in the fridge, three months frozen.
tips: Wet your hands slightly before rolling and nothing sticks.
This is one recipe where dates cannot be swapped for stevia or monk fruit - they are structural. If you want it lower sugar, use half dates and add 2 tbsp more nut butter to hold it together.
A pinch of espresso powder with the cocoa makes them taste much more chocolatey.
health_notes: Dates bring fibre and potassium along with their sugar, which is not the same thing as eating a spoon of syrup - but they are still dense. One or two is a snack; six is dessert.

source.adapted: Standard date-and-nut ball, with the maple syrup most versions add left out entirely.
